dedupe_keys.name: zambia motorised travel time to the nearest health facility cpas 100 m raster in seconds public transport speeds on all weather roads and walking elsewhere

description: This raster shows, for every 100-metre cell in Zambia, how many seconds it takes to reach the nearest health facility by the kind of transport available to poor households. It was produced by the Child Poverty and Access to Services (CPAS) project of the Data for Children Collaborative and published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. Travel times assume local public transport speeds on all-weather and asphalt roads and walking speeds on all other roads, tracks, paths and land cover, and were computed with the open CPAS software, whose method is described in a Scientific Data paper. Coverage is the whole of Zambia as of August 2024. The GeoTIFF is free and available to download (about 940 MB) under CC BY. Caveats: it is a single-country snapshot, the facility list and speed assumptions follow the CPAS method and may differ from national data, and seasonal flooding of unpaved roads is not modelled. Simulation uses: estimating how road or bridge loss in floods lengthens access to care, targeting outreach services to remote children, and weighting exposure analysis by access. Related records: the HeiGIT accessibility indicators (data-heigit-accessibility-indicators) and AccessMod (model-accessmod) produce comparable access measures, and the Malawi modelled facility catchments (data-malawi-modelled-health-facility-catchments) cover a neighbouring country.
